text:
Anjali Shah: heads-up — we're seeing a spike in backend QPS tied to a sudden drop in prefix cache hit-rate, started ~08:12 UTC
Tom Nguyen: seeing it too on dashboards. KV cache hit-rate down from ~86% to ~22% for recent traffic window. p99 token latency jumped from 120ms -> 520ms.
Priya Rao: any recent deploys touching cache keying or prompt surface? I didn't push anything that touches key generation.
Miguel Alvarez: I rolled a small change to add tool-call metadata into the request body 45m ago (not supposed to affect cache keying because we only key on normalized prefix). but the tokenizer update yesterday might have changed whitespace normalization.
Anjali Shah: attaching quick grep of logs (truncated):
```
2026-03-17T08:11:53Z INFO cache.miss key="pfx:8f3a9..." size=128
2026-03-17T08:11:53Z INFO cache.miss key="pfx:8f3a9..." size=129
2026-03-17T08:11:54Z WARN serve.forward congested backend_qps=520
2026-03-17T08:11:55Z INFO cache.populate key="pfx:47b1..." ttl=300
```
Tom Nguyen: logs show many near-duplicate keys with tiny differences (length variance by 1-3 chars). Looks like whitespace or special token differences causing mismatch.
Priya Rao: confirmed via profiler: tokenization divergence introduced a non-deterministic space in some system messages. That explains the mass of unique cache keys.
SRE Lin: consequence: KV miss storm caused backend replicas to spin up, hitting kernel selection paths and saturating our GPU RPC queue; batching heuristics got worse since they were trying to batch newly arriving long sequences.
Miguel Alvarez: immediate mitigation options: 1) emergency disable prefix caching 2) patch key normalization and roll 3) apply temporary rate-limit on miss-induced backend QPS. Which do we want now?
Anjali Shah: let's avoid full disable if possible — that will blow cost up and increase latency even more. Start small: push a config change to dedupe keys by normalizing whitespace on the cache key generation path (strip multiple spaces, collapse special markers). Can we hotfix that?
Tom Nguyen: I can push normalization code to the cache key pipeline and roll to 10% traffic in ~8 minutes. Also enabling a soft fail-fast: if miss-rate for a single prefix > 50% within 30s, route to a fallback model variant with local LRU.
Priya Rao: while the canary is rolling, I'll pre-warm the cache for the top 200 affected prefixes using historical payloads to rehydrate hits. Also toggle the batcher target window to 15ms to reduce simultaneous miss bounces.
ops-bot: deploy-bot reports: started canary rollout of cache-key-normalize v1 -> 10% at 08:22 UTC
SRE Lin: add a circuit-breaker on cache service responses — if Redis latency > 200ms or error rate > 5%, stop waiting and pass-through to backend to prevent queue jam.
Miguel Alvarez: quick experiment results from canary: hit-rate for canary cohort improved 82% -> 89% after normalization, p95 latency down ~35%. Backend QPS for canary lowered by ~48%.
Anjali Shah: great. escalate to 50% and keep monitoring — don't do 100% yet until we confirm tokenizer determinism fix.
Tom Nguyen: rolling to 50% now. Also I tweaked batching heuristics to prefer small micro-batches for identifiers that historically had high miss churn. That dropped tokens-per-GPU spike by ~30%.
Priya Rao: tokenizer commit with deterministic whitespace normalization is ready for code-review; if merged we can flip full normalization at key-gen and then revert the temporary canary settings.
SRE Lin: postmortem action items (quick notes): 1) add a fuzz-test for tokenization->cache-key invariance 2) add hit-rate alert (absolute drop by >20% within 5m) 3) pre-warm job for top N prefixes after deploys that touch system prompts 4) improve cache metrics by prefix hash buckets
Miguel Alvarez: also consider adding probabilistic bloom-keying to reduce sensitivity to tiny changes (i.e., hash the normalized prefix with low-res fingerprint and tolerate small diffs).
Anjali Shah: agree on all. For immediate incident close: normalization canary -> 50% -> observed improvement -> escalate to 100% at 08:33 UTC. We left emergency disable off.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: normalization v1 -> 100% completed at 08:33:42 UTC
Tom Nguyen: final checks: global hit-rate recovered to ~84% after 10m, p99 latency back to ~150ms, no more backend autoscale churn.
Priya Rao: follow-up: I'll add a nightly job that builds a warmup snapshot for top 1k prefixes across customers so we don't get cold waves after infra changes.
SRE Lin: filing incident ticket: INC-2026-0317-prefix-cache-miss-wave. We'll schedule a formal postmortem with timelines and RCA.
Anjali Shah: thanks everyone — nice quick coordination. We'll keep the alert thresholds conservative going forward. :thumbsup:
